comparisons.peer_topic: Adaptive Computing and Embedded Systems Portfolio Expansion
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD expanded its adaptive computing portfolio with the launch of Versal Series Gen 2 devices, including Versal AI Edge and Prime Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, which integrate preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD identify the shift to edge computing and AI as a primary market driver. Intel describes the Internet shifting to 'cloud-to-edge infrastructure' with 'exponential' demand for high-performance computing at the edge driven by AI. Similarly, AMD highlights the expansion of its 'Versal AI Edge' adaptive SoCs, which integrate 'preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing' for 'end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems,' reflecting a shared focus on bringing AI capabilities to the edge.

sentences.text: The Internet is undergoing a shift toward a cloud-to-edge infrastructure, combining unrivaled scale and capacity in the cloud with faster response times at nearby edges.
As AI is transforming and automating every industry-from factories to smart cities to hospitals-the demand for high-performance computing at the edge has expanded exponentially.

We expanded our adaptive computing portfolio with differentiated solutions with the launch of the new Versal™ Series Gen 2 devices, including the new Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 and Versal Prime Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, which bring preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing together in a single device for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems.

comparisons.peer_topic: Global Technology Scope and Product Portfolio
comparisons.peer_summary: Avago is a global technology leader designing semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions, including AI networking, home connectivity, and software for mainframe and cloud platforms, while also offering fibre channel storage area networking products.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies frame their strategies around a shift to cloud-edge architectures. Intel cites the Internet's shift to 'cloud-to-edge infrastructure' to combine cloud scale with edge response times. Avago similarly describes its infrastructure software solutions as enabling customers to manage applications across 'private and hybrid cloud' platforms and explicitly includes 'software-defined edge' in its portfolio description.

sentences.text: The Internet is undergoing a shift toward a cloud-to-edge infrastructure, combining unrivaled scale and capacity in the cloud with faster response times at nearby edges.

Our infrastructure software solutions help enterprises simplify their information technology environments so they can increase business velocity and flexibility, and enable customers to plan, develop, deliver, automate, manage and secure applications across mainframe, distributed, edge, mobile, and private and hybrid cloud platforms.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company experienced substantial improvements in pricing and margins in 2024, driven by increased demand growth partly from AI deployment, normal customer inventories, and industry supply discipline.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies cite AI deployment as a critical growth driver in 2024, though they operate in different segments of the supply chain. Intel attributes the exponential expansion of edge computing demand to AI transforming industries. Micron reports that 'increasing demand growth' and improved pricing/margins in 2024 were 'driven in part by deployment of AI,' indicating that AI is fueling demand for high-performance computing infrastructure at both the processor (Intel) and memory (Micron) levels.

sentences.text: As AI is transforming and automating every industry-from factories to smart cities to hospitals-the demand for high-performance computing at the edge has expanded exponentially.

Increasing demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI and mostly normal customer inventories, combined with industry-wide supply discipline, resulted in an industry supply and demand balance that substantially improved from 2023 conditions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Segment Financial Performance and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2024 increased 217%, driven by strong demand from enterprise software, consumer internet applications, and industry verticals like automotive, financial services, and healthcare, with compute revenue up 244% and networking revenue up 133%.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify the rapid expansion of AI-driven demand as a key market shift. Intel states that the demand for 'high-performance computing at the edge has expanded exponentially' as 'AI is transforming and automating every industry.' NVIDIA corroborates this trend in its Data Center segment, which saw revenue increase 217% driven by strong demand for 'AI infrastructure' accessed both through the cloud and on-premises, validating the broad industry shift toward accelerated computing for AI.

sentences.text: As AI is transforming and automating every industry-from factories to smart cities to hospitals-the demand for high-performance computing at the edge has expanded exponentially.

Customers across industry verticals access NVIDIA AI infrastructure both through the cloud and on-premises.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm believes that 5G, combined with high-performance computing and on-device AI, will drive adoption in automotive and IoT sectors, and that maintaining leadership in 5G technology development, standardization, and IP licensing is critical for long-term business sustainability.

Intel describes the Internet shifting to 'cloud-to-edge infrastructure' combining cloud scale with edge response times. Qualcomm mirrors this by believing that '5G combined with high-performance, low-power computing and on-device artificial intelligence will continue to drive adoption' in automotive and IoT sectors, highlighting a shared strategic belief in the integration of network and compute capabilities at the edge.
